study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping Neurophysiological Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder Using Normative Models of the Functional Connectome

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used the DIDA-MDD (Disease Imaging Data Archiving - Major Depressive Disorder Working Group) dataset, which consists of rs-fMRI data from 9 research centers (10 datasets): CMU (China Medical University, Shenyang), CSU (Central South University, Changsha), GCMU1 (Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine, dataset 1), GCMU2 (Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine, dataset 2), KMU (Kunming Medical University, Kunming), PKU (Peking University Sixth Hospital, Beijing), SCU (Sichuan University, Chengdu), SWU (Southwest University, Chongqing), YMU (National Yang-Ming University, Taipei), and ZZU (Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou). GCMU1 and GCMU2 were collected using the same scanner at one site with different scan parameters. Total participants: 2227 (1148 MDD patients + 1079 HCs).

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: All 1079 HCs were used to build normative models of functional connectivity strength (FCS) via Gaussian process regression with age and sex as covariates. 10-fold cross-validation was first performed on HCs to assess model generalizability, then the final normative models were trained on all HCs. 1148 MDD patients were used for individual deviation analysis and neurophysiological subtyping using k-means clustering. A subsample of 43 MDD patients from CSU received 6-month paroxetine treatment for treatment outcome prediction analysis using support vector regression.

model-1.model-name: Gaussian process regression normative model of FCS

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built for each brain region using Gaussian process regression (GPR) with age and sex as covariates. 10-fold cross-validation was first used to evaluate generalizability on the 1079 HCs (SMSE close to 1: 0.996 +/- 0.013; MSLL close to 0: -0.001 +/- 0.007). Then the final normative models were trained on all 1079 HCs for subsequent MDD deviation analyses. Since the final model was trained on all HCs without a held-out test set, overall-phase equals train-phase.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The weighted mean age was computed across all 10 HC datasets (9 centers, 10 datasets) using: sum(N_i * mean_i) / sum(N_i) = 33.96 years. The pooled SD was computed using: sqrt(sum((N_i - 1) * SD_i^2) / sum(N_i - 1)) = 11.40 years. Per-center HC data: CMU (N=248, 27.25 +/- 8.22), CSU (N=108, 32.31 +/- 7.96), GCMU1 (N=34, 30.09 +/- 10.88), GCMU2 (N=66, 29.33 +/- 10.12), KMU (N=46, 39.02 +/- 12.20), PKU (N=73, 31.90 +/- 9.01), SCU (N=41, 34.83 +/- 17.69), SWU (N=254, 39.65 +/- 15.80), YMU (N=109, 51.12 +/- 11.70), ZZU (N=100, 22.43 +/- 4.49). The overall dataset age range is reported as 11-93 years but this includes both MDD and HC participants; HC-specific min/max is not reported. The train-phase equals the overall-phase since the final model was trained on all HCs.
